title: AlgoExpert · Min Number Of Coins For Change

slides.heading: Min Number Of Coins For Change
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Dynamic Programming
slides.narration: Let's solve Min Number Of Coins For Change, a medium dynamic programming problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Fewest coins summing to n, or -1 if impossible.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Fewest coins summing to n, or -1 if impossible.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Build the fewest coins for every amount from zero up to n.
slides.narration: Build the fewest coins for every amount from zero up to n.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Greedy (largest coin first) can fail, e.g. coins [1, 3, 4], n = 6
Bottom-up DP → O(n · d) time, O(n) space
slides.narration: Greedy, always taking the biggest coin, fails for coins like one, three and four with six: greedy gives four, one, one, but three plus three is better. Recursion explores exponentially many choices. A bottom-up table over amounts takes n times the number of coins.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Array of infinities, zero for amount zero
2. For each coin, relax amounts from the coin up
slides.narration: Step by step. First, array of infinities, zero for amount zero. Second, for each coin, relax amounts from the coin up. Third, answer or minus one.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: After coin 1: dp = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]
slides.narration: Processing coin 1: each amount from 1 up tries using one 1-coin plus the best for the remainder. Now seven needs 7 coins.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: After coin 5: dp = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3]
slides.narration: Processing coin 5: each amount from 5 up tries using one 5-coin plus the best for the remainder. Now seven needs 3 coins.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Coin 10 is too big
slides.narration: Coin 10 is bigger than 7, so it can't help.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We fill dp with max value and set dp of zero to zero. For each coin, for each amount from the coin up, if the remainder is reachable we take the min with one more coin. Finally we map max value to minus one.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n times d. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
slides.narration: Zero needs zero coins, unreachable amounts return minus one, and you must check for infinity before adding one, to avoid overflow.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: return the actual coins (store choices)
slides.narration: Show the greedy counterexample early. A follow-up returns the coins themselves by storing the last coin used per amount.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Build the fewest coins for every amount from zero up to n.
slides.narration: To recap Min Number Of Coins For Change: Build the fewest coins for every amount from zero up to n. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
